decisions.executionNote: Coin is in left workspace, bank on right. Begin elbow-up left approach with open gripper, raising and orienting toward a downward pinch.
Replan smaller rotations after continuity rejection; curl upward while advancing left toward the coin.
Advance toward left holder with gradual downward orientation and maintained elbow-up bend.
Continue controlled left advance above holder; keep jaws open while turning into top-down grasp.
Approach above the left coin while completing downward wrist orientation, maintaining joint continuity.
Finish top-down alignment above the holder, then use close wrist view to center and orient the coin between jaws.
Use wrist feedback to shift toward the off-center coin and align jaw normals with its faces; remain above the holder.
Coin nearly centered; make a small lateral/yaw correction and begin closing onto its exposed faces without moving the holder.
Correct the final lateral offset visible in the wrist view and lower a few millimeters before fully pinching.
Close fully on the coin, then lift gently to check retention against the stationary holder.
Lift the closed left gripper above eight centimeters, checking the gold coin remains between the jaws and separates from the holder.
The coin stayed in the holder; reopen and descend for a deeper, centered pinch rather than assuming retention.
Lower another 18 mm to bring the exposed coin well into the finger contact region, then close gradually while centered.
Hold the deeper pinch closed long enough for the fingers to settle, then start a small retention-test lift.
Maintain full closure and lift slowly, using relative coin and holder motion to verify the new grasp.
Coin still appears seated. Reopen and offset the pinch along the coin plane so the exposed rim is inside, rather than behind, the fingertips.
Coin has moved beside the holder and turned face-on. Recenter over its new visible position with open fingers before attempting recovery.
Approach the now-flat coin from above, positioning the finger tips at its rim and narrowing the opening cautiously above the table.
Center the flat coin laterally between the fingers, then close at the current tabletop height without pushing farther downward.
The coin is tilting between the closing fingers. Maintain full closure and make a slow test lift to check capture.
Keep the rim pinch closed and lift clear of the holder; verify that the coin follows the fingers rather than the table.
The coin did not follow the lift. Reopen and approach its flat rim with the grasp center shifted forward and lower to tabletop level.
Lower the open fingers carefully to the flat coin's rim while narrowing the aperture, avoiding further lateral pushing.
At tabletop contact, stop descending and close fully around the centered rim; allow the gripper to settle before testing lift.
Test the settled rim grasp with a slow vertical lift, keeping the fingers fully closed and watching for separation from the holder.
Reposition the open pinch over the coin's center rather than its near rim, then return slowly to tabletop contact for a more complete capture.
Close fully with the coin centered at the finger tips; pause at the contact height to let both jaws settle around its rim.
Both jaws now visibly straddle the coin diameter. Maintain closure, settle, and lift a short distance to verify retention.
The coin now stays fixed between the jaws while the holder recedes. Lift it clear, keeping full closure for transfer to the right workspace.
Coin retention is visible. Turn the left wrist gradually toward a central handover, preserving the rim grasp and elbow-up configuration.
Bring the held disk upright for a perpendicular central handover; start raising and yawing the open right receiver in its own workspace.
Continue upright coin transport and elbow-up receiver approach, with both arms separated and the left grasp held closed.
Continue toward the central perpendicular handover, holding the coin upright while the open receiver turns inward.
Continue slow coordinated positioning, keeping a gap between the receiver and coin until the disk is upright.
Finish turning the disk upright and bring the open right jaws toward the handover height, maintaining clearance from the left fingers.
Complete the upright perpendicular handover pose; align right jaw direction and lateral height before closing the remaining approach gap.
Hold the upright coin steady while the open right gripper advances perpendicular to its plane, stopping short for visual alignment.
Narrow and slightly raise the receiving jaws to pinch the exposed upper coin edge while avoiding the left holding fingers.
Advance the narrowed right jaws a few millimeters onto the coin's exposed face and close fully, keeping the left grasp until capture is secure.
Let the right pinch settle, then gradually release the left fingers and make a tiny separating lift to verify the transfer.
The coin slipped during transfer. Open and separate both grippers to avoid batting it, then reacquire its resting position from the cameras.
Move the left gripper aside and turn toward a recovery approach, exposing the coin's landing area without crossing either arm.
Reduce the left retreat and rotation increments after the continuity rejection; expose the dropped coin while maintaining the current elbow branch.
Continue left clearance and slow downward reorientation, revealing the coin near the central-left tabletop for recovery.
Angle the left wrist down toward the central tabletop to locate the slipped coin, keeping both grippers open and separated.
The gold disk is visible at the lower wrist edge. Continue slow top-down alignment over the central-left recovery area.
The dropped coin is visible on the table. Complete more of the top-down orientation before making a precise centering translation.
Use the visible coin location to bring the left open gripper above it while completing the downward approach, with the right arm stationary and clear.
Finish orienting down above the coin in the central-left workspace, maintaining clearance before the final tabletop approach.
Move the right arm away from the recovery approach. Lower and center the open left fingers over the flat coin while preserving arm separation.
Center the flat disk across the finger tips at the proven tabletop height, close fully, and settle before any recovery lift.
Allow the centered rim pinch to settle, then make a short vertical retention test with the left fingers fully closed.
The rim capture slipped behind the tips. Reopen and offset the grasp along the disk plane to place its center in the contact region before reclosing.
Fine-center the flat coin just beyond the finger apexes at tabletop height, then close on both sides of its diameter.
The coin is centered across both finger contacts. Keep full closure and lift slowly to verify a stable recovery grasp.
The disk again stayed on the table. Shift the open grasp slightly through its center and lower to the rim so both contacts capture the full diameter.
Close symmetrically on the now-centered disk at the current height, with no translation until the rim contacts settle.
Keep the rim clamped and introduce a very slight cant during a slow lift to retain the thin disk rather than letting it slip past the finger ends.
Reopen after the rim slipped and align the wrist to the slight oblique angle that previously retained the flat coin, before recentering its exposed disk.
Move the open pinch back over the visible disk so its center lies just beyond the finger apexes, while descending to the prior successful contact height.
Fine-tune the disk center by a few millimeters and close symmetrically at fixed height, allowing both rim contacts to settle.
The disk tilted out toward the front of the contact area. Reopen enough to place the fingers farther across its diameter, then close without descending farther.
